problem_summary.summary: Check whether two equal-length strings have a consistent one-to-one character mapping in the same position order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: equal-length strings s and t of ASCII characters. Return whether each character in s maps to exactly one character in t and no two source characters map to the same target character.
constraints: s and t contain valid ASCII characters

brute_force.explanation: Check every pair of positions. The pair must contain the same character in s exactly when it contains the same character in t.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A valid bijection preserves both equalities and inequalities between every pair of positions. Checking all pairs therefore rejects exactly the strings whose repetition patterns differ.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2), checking every pair of positions.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary, using only scalar values.

optimized.explanation: Track the most recent position of each ASCII character in both strings. At every index, the two characters must have matching previous-occurrence positions; then record the current position.
optimized.correctness_idea: Matching previous-occurrence positions means the two characters either both appeared before at the same last position or both are new. This enforces consistent forward and reverse mappings.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n), one pass through the strings.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary: two fixed-size arrays for the 128 ASCII values.

steps.action: Record position marker 1 for both characters.
Record position marker 2 for both characters.

steps.condition: Both characters last appeared at marker 2.
Both characters last appeared at marker 1.
steps.action: Record marker 4; scan completes and returns true.

edge_cases.case: A repeated source character maps inconsistently
edge_cases.handling: Its previous marker differs from the target's marker, so false is returned.

edge_cases.case: Two source characters would share one target
edge_cases.handling: The target's previous marker differs from the new source character's marker, so false is returned.

edge_cases.case: Every character is distinct at each position
edge_cases.handling: All prior markers are zero and the strings are accepted.
